messages:
Reese: quick spike idea: add a 'scrub-preview' feature so tenants can see redaction results on a tiny sample before flipping digest on. less surprises during rollouts. thoughts?

Maria: yes please. PMs hate when customers enable and then freak out. preview should not leak raw text to console unless tenant opts in and signs DPA.

Ankit: from UI side we can show side-by-side: original (blacked/hashed) + scrubbed digest. but we must ensure console preview itself obeys RBAC and TTL.

Jamal: important: previews must apply exact same redaction pipeline as production (regex -> schema -> hmac). otherwise it's worthless. will prototype a dockerized pipeline test.

Sasha: edgecases: tool outputs that embed emails inside base64 or nested objects break simple regex. preview needs schema-aware parsers for json, protobuf and common extension types.

Nadia: propose preview limits: max 100 samples/day per tenant; only first 10 can show original raw if tenant gave legal consent. otherwise show hashed/pseudonymized values.

Reese: good. also add a CLI for ops/SEs to run a one-off preview for a customer:

```bash
redwood-cli logging preview --tenant tenant_123 --route gallery --limit 5 --raw-allowed=true
```

Maria: for auditing add `preview_request_id` to the audit-log entry and require justification. SREs should be able to query `audit.preview_requests` with filters.

Ankit: telemetry we need: `preview.count`, `preview.raw_view_count`, `preview.error_rate`, `preview.redact_mismatch_rate`. these feed the rollout decisions and alerting.

Jamal: mismatch_rate is key. If preview shows pipeline vs production differences > 0.05% -> block rollout. We can compute by hashing fields and comparing.

Sasha: attachments again: previews must never include binary blobs. show metadata only (mime/size/sha256). any raw image must be blurred/placeholder.

Nadia: export flow: customers with legal approval can request a secure export of full-inspect bundles (S3 with KMS + short presigned url). we should add an approvals workflow in console.

Reese: security note: exports must require multi-approver sign-off for high-risk tenants, and retention TTL default 7 days. also log exporter actor and IP.

Ankit: UI idea: when enabling digest, show an estimated monthly cost delta using `est_cost_reduction_pct` from telemetry and sample payload-size histogram. helps PMs and customers.

Maria: rollout plan: feature flag `scrub_preview.v1` with staged percents, but preview UI behind permission `logging.preview:view`. Add an enterprise toggle for customers to enable internal-only raw preview.

Jamal: key management for pseudonymization: HMAC per-tenant with key-kid in metadata. rotation path: we keep previous key-kids for verification and mark digests with key-kid. Re-hashing historical data optional via backfill job.

Sasha: can we add a short circuit for embeddings failures: if embedding pipeline errors, we store the 1-line original snippet in the digest (but hashed) to aid debugging, and open an incident. elevated logging only for a small percent.

Nadia: alerts: if `preview.error_rate > 0.2%` for 10m -> notify #eng-oncall and pause any automatic rollout. if `preview.raw_view_count` spikes unexpectedly -> alert SecOps.

Reese: ops-bot will start a staging run for scrub-preview with tenant-mock routes and report back in ~20m. @ops-bot kick it off.

ops-bot: scrub-preview canary: started for staging. sampling=10, raw_preview=false, limit=5. will post metrics: preview.count, preview.raw_view_count, preview.mismatch_rate in 20m. :robot_face:

Maria: last thing: add a tiny banner in console preview: "This is a preview. Data may be pseudonymized. For full export contact legal." avoids confusion.

Ankit: action items: (1) PoC redaction-parity tests (jamal/sasha) (2) preview UI + RBAC + banner (ankit/maria) (3) HMAC key-kid lifecycle (nadia) (4) ops canary + alerts (reese/ops). reconvene after canary results.

Jamal: linking a rough test plan in case useful: https://redwood.dev/internal/logging/scrub-preview-test-plan (WIP). ping me for test vectors.

Sasha: I'll share the prod-ish payload corpus that broke our old heuristics. thanks all :thumbsup:
